Sierra / Ops team —

Thanks again for the conversation this morning. Per our mutual action plan (MAP) conversation, I put together a concise final-mile checklist so we can lock capacity and align acceptance gates between evaluation and production. High-level items: 

- Staging pool: 8 H100 (quantized profile Q4) for the 4-week eval; production tranche: 32 H100.
- Lead times: Dedicated cloud pool (Redwood Dedicated) can be spun within ~6 weeks once PO is in; Private on-prem delivery (customer-provisioned rack) currently averages 12–14 weeks from PO to handed-over nodes.
- Acceptance gates: 1) Canaries (throughput/latency SLO), 2) Data-path/policy validation, 3) Ramp test (steady-state 72h at 75% sustained QPS).
- Eval schedule: start eval week of Nov 16; canary week Nov 30; production handover target Dec 21 (to meet Q1 launch).

Ask: If Nov 30 canary window is acceptable, please confirm PO intent by Nov 13 so we can allocate the staging tranche and pin the dedicated pool. If Nov 13 is tight, let us know the preferred sign-off date and we will present a tranche hedge option.

I've attached a simple checklist and the GPU sizing model so your infra and procurement teams can validate numbers quickly.

Thanks,
Markus
Markus Klein
Head of Strategic Accounts — Redwood Inference

Quick notes on the operational constraints and swap window: 

- Swap from Dedicated -> Private: technically straightforward if the private hardware matches the same instance profile (H100, same quantization settings). The risk is scheduling — a late private handover requires us to keep the dedicated pool warm for up to 6 weeks while racks are provisioned. That warm pool costs show up as committed but we can offer a step-down billing mechanism in the MAP (50% fallback rate for the first 4 weeks post-handover).
- Procurement windows: for Private (rack delivery) E2E we need 12–14 weeks if the customer is responsible for hardware procurement; if Redwood handles the hardware order through our partners it shortens to ~9–10 weeks but requires a hardware procurement addendum and different billing cadence.
- Acceptance gating: propose we make the ramp test criteria explicit in the MAP doc: 95th latency < 220ms @ 4k token median; token cost delta within 5% of baseline model. Also include a rollback policy and retained KV cache snapshot for the first 48 hours post-handover.

I can draft the operational appendix for the MAP (swapping steps, warm-pool accounting, rollback runbook). Markus — give me the PO intent date and I'll model the tranche cost for both pathways.

Karthik
Principal, Capacity Partnerships — Redwood Inference
